about.body: The N63 is BMW's 4.4-litre twin-turbocharged V8 petrol engine, in production since 2008. It was BMW's first petrol V8 with a "hot-vee" design — the turbochargers positioned inside the V between the cylinder banks rather than on the outside of the engine. It's fitted across four BMW model lines: the 6 Series 650i, the 8 Series 850i, and the X5 and X6 xDrive50i. This is the engine that underpins BMW's V8-powered mainstream models (as opposed to the higher-output S63 versions found in M-badged cars like the M5 and M8, which are related but not the same engine).

byModel.body: Across the 6 Series, the N63 powered the 650i in its F06/F12/F13 generation (2011–2018), covering the coupe, convertible and Gran Coupe body styles. The 8 Series continues the pattern with the 850i in its current G14/G15/G16 generation (2018–present). Across the SUV range, the N63 appears in the X5 xDrive50i (E70 and F15, 2009–2018) and the X6 xDrive50i (E71 and F16, 2009–2019).

compatibility.body: Because the N63 spans four different models and multiple generations, compatibility comes down to confirming your exact model, generation, and drivetrain spec — which we do by registration. The hot-vee turbocharger placement is consistent across all N63 applications, but ancillaries, mounting, and cooling system configuration differ by model and generation.
